statement: In mechanics and geometry, the 3D rotation group, denoted $\mathrm{SO}(3)$, is the group of all rotations about the origin of three-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^3$, whose matrix representations satisfy the orthogonality condition $A^T A = I$ with $A \in \mathrm{SO}(3)$.

symbols.meaning: 3D rotation group of all rotations about the origin

properties.property: The Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ consists of all skew-symmetric $3 \times 3$ matrices with Lie bracket given by the commutator $[A_1, A_2] = A_1 A_2 - A_2 A_1$.
properties.why: Differentiating the orthogonality condition $A^T A = I$ for $A \in \mathrm{SO}(3)$ yields skew-symmetric matrices as the tangent space at the identity.

properties.property: The Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ (with commutator) is isomorphic to the Lie algebra $\mathbb{R}^3$ (with cross product).
properties.why: The infinitesimal generator action satisfies $\left.\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\phi}\right|_{\phi=0} R(\phi, \boldsymbol{n})\boldsymbol{u} = \boldsymbol{n} \times \boldsymbol{u}$, mapping Euler vector $\boldsymbol{\omega} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ to the linear map $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\omega}}(\boldsymbol{u}) = \boldsymbol{\omega} \times \boldsymbol{u}$.

properties.property: Under the hat-map $\boldsymbol{\omega} \mapsto \widehat{\boldsymbol{\omega}} = \boldsymbol{\omega} \cdot \boldsymbol{L}$, the bracket satisfies $[\widehat{\boldsymbol{u}}, \widehat{\boldsymbol{v}}] = \widehat{\boldsymbol{u} \times \boldsymbol{v}}$ and $\widehat{\boldsymbol{u}}\boldsymbol{v} = \boldsymbol{u} \times \boldsymbol{v}$.
properties.why: The commutation relations $[L_x, L_y] = L_z, [L_z, L_x] = L_y, [L_y, L_z] = L_x$ agree with the cross product of standard unit vectors in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

properties.property: Rotations $g_\phi$ about the $z$-axis and $g_\theta$ about the $x$-axis generate all of $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ and correspond to Möbius transformations on $\mathbb{C}$.
properties.why: Bilinear transformations on the stereographic projection plane compose according to matrix multiplication in $\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{C})$.

properties.property: There is a smooth, 2:1 surjective group homomorphism $p: \mathrm{SU}(2) \to \mathrm{SO}(3)$.
properties.why: Each rotation corresponds to a pair of matrices $\pm \Pi_u(g) \in \mathrm{SU}(2)$, making $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ the universal covering group of $\mathrm{SO}(3)$.

assumptions.assumption: Transformations are origin-preserving linear maps of three-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^3$.
assumptions.breaks_when: Transformations include non-zero translations (affine rigid-body motions) or act on curved/non-Euclidean manifolds.

assumptions.assumption: Matrix representations preserve Euclidean metric orthogonality via $A^T A = I$.
assumptions.breaks_when: Transformations include non-isometric scaling, shear, or non-orthogonal distortions.

failure_modes.mode: Two-to-one sign ambiguity in SU(2) parameterization
failure_modes.signature: Two distinct unitary matrices $\pm \Pi_u(g)$ represent the identical rotation $g \in \mathrm{SO}(3)$.
failure_modes.cause: The covering projection $p: \mathrm{SU}(2) \to \mathrm{SO}(3)$ has a two-element kernel $\{I, -I\}$.

failure_modes.mode: Axis vector singularity in cross product / hat-map multiplication
failure_modes.cause: Any vector $\boldsymbol{u}$ lies in the null space of its corresponding skew-symmetric matrix $\widehat{\boldsymbol{u}}$ because $\boldsymbol{u} \times \boldsymbol{u} = \boldsymbol{0}$.
